payload.rebuttal: argued: git's own diff output is always produced in tree (lexicographic) order, independent of the order the pathspec arguments are passed after `--`. I confirmed this by running `git diff A B -- z m a` and `git diff A B -- a m z` on the same two commits: both printed the same three `diff --git` blocks in the same order. So `sorted(review_paths & baseline_paths)` and `list(review_paths & baseline_paths)` produce byte-identical `git diff` output for every input, because git re-sorts the paths itself before generating output regardless of what order they arrive in. No test, however constructed, can observe a difference between the two through this function's return value, so the mutant's survival does not indicate a verification gap. I kept `sorted()` as the implementation, since it still matches the letter of the spec and keeps the python-level list deterministic, but did not add a test for it, since none can distinguish it from `list()`.
